Dead Space was the very first seventh generation game I played. I remember being absolutely floored as I booted it up to look at the gorgeous view of the Ishimura and Aegis VII. To say that its visuals hold up today would be a lie in terms of its textures, but the atmosphere and visual style is absolutely timeless.

Dead Space bleeds creativity and inspiration in nearly every facet of its creation. While very obviously hearkening after Resident Evil 4, it's far, far more than shooting zombies in space. I've replayed this game so many times that I know almost every jump scare by heart, yet even still, it somehow managed to leave me unsettled. Dead Space interweaves its plot and its gameplay both with horror, never content to follow anything 'by the book,' yet cultivating its inspiration from RE4 in brilliant setpieces.

I could write page after page about how good Dead Space is, but it would ruin so much of what make it great. The sound design, the music, the haunting story, are all things that are best experienced in the moment, when you're frantic and only a few shots away from an empty inventory. As you sprint through hallways, ducking and weaving around enemies, smashing boxes for just a single ammo drop. 

Dead Space is an exquisite experience, and one of the finest horror games ever made.

This game caught me off guard, back when it released, I didn't expect EA of all studio's to drop a true rival to the Resident Evil series, but they pulled it off. The game pure drips atmosphere especially the sound scape and monster designs. The ship feels like a haunted house in space, very reminisent of the movie Event Horizon.

Its a decent length too, some puzzle's but nothing to get stuck on. Graphics stand up, still looks great in my opinion. It's not perfect either though, it's a little too action packed which ends up making it not as scary, but I could level the same criticism at RE4-6. Also it has a fair few weapons but you probably won't use them much (or at all, like me) as the cutter you get at the start is fine for the whole game when upgraded and there's ammo for it everywhere. There's a new game+ mode which is great, except it's rendered utterly pointless as you re-start with everything from your last play as well as a bunch of bonus stuff for finishing the game but you can't change difficultly. So its exactly the same except miles easier.

The game runs really well but you need to tweak it a little. Disable AA in game as it makes it look really blurry, also disable V-sync or it locks you at 30fps. In your graphics cards control panel, force AA and V-sync from there and lock frame-rate at 60, over 60 corpse's and boxes start to float if you touch them and really high frame-rates totally break it, invisible walls and such.

Overall, still a great, very addictive game. Not quite a good as the Resi games but a pretty damn good next best thing.

Without going too much into spoilers for the OG game, we play as our favorite pushover silent protagonist CEC Engineer Isaac Clarke, an everyday space Joe trying to make a living who finds himself stranded on a massive deep-space mining ship known as the USG Ishimura that went dark & overrun by a hostile alien scourge called the Necromorphs, where he's forced to engage in a desperate fight for survival as he searches for his lost girlfriend, Dr. Nicole Brennan. Trapped alongside other fellow crew members of the USG Kellion, Chief Security Officer Zack Hammond & Computer Specialist Kendra Daniels, you uncover a dark, horrific truth of a strange alien artifact retrieved by the Ishimura crew earlier, known as the Marker.

Gameplay is just as fun & thrilling as I remembered; instead of shooting mutated humanoid alien space monsters in the head like most zombie games, you cut the limbs off of Necromorphs to permanently put them down for good with nothing but engineering work tools as improvised weapons like the iconic Plasma Cutter, a standard-issue industrial mining tool used to carve through solid rock & metals in the most "Cut Off Their Limbs" bloodbath fashion. Isaac Clarke is an engineer after all, not a soldier. Plus, the Atmosphere in the Original 2008 version is much creepier than in the 2023 Remake due to Isaac Clarke being mostly a silent protagonist, adding more to the dread vibe that awaits you in the dark corners of the USG Ishimura ship as you hear Isaac's heart beating in fear & makes you feel like you're in his shoes.

Graphically, for a game released back in 2008, it still holds up decently well for the most part, despite the Dead Space 2023 Remake. If you're looking for an Original Dead Space experience, the 2008 version is the way to go! I still play it to this day & the Remake back & forth; always got to appreciate the Original for what it was!

NOTE: The Steam version of Dead Space (2008) does NOT include any of the DLCs, like the console versions on the PlayStation 3 & XBOX 360. So, you will be playing the PC version in a vanilla fashion.

Ending my review here,
Video game director/producer Glen Schofield & the original studio Visceral Games (formerly known as EA Redwood Shores) created one of the most iconic Sci-Fi Survival Horror franchises ever made with Dead Space. I'm proud to be serving aboard the USG Ishimura for years since then.

BONUS: There's a message hidden in plain sight for both Dead Space (2008) & Dead Space 2023 Remake! Once you see it, you'll be surprised.

You'll navigate a grim spaceship to slowly unveil a disturbing plot with unexpected twists, fighting and dismembering through horrid monstrosities that are waiting to jump you from every corner, every ceiling, every hole in the wall in this gore-filled adventure, and if you didn't play this back in the days, I can say you will most likely not be disappointed by playing it now.

Deep with endless skies and stars, black with emptiness and fears. As you keep opening your eyes soon you realise there nowhere to run or hide. The pace invaded your mind and you realise how small you are in this “place”. 
You as Isaac Clarke a space engineer set to investigate damned spaceship Ishimura. With your skills and tools you have to find out why this ship became so silent from inside. Beyond your first step you soon start to feel dreadful emotions. You hands starts to shake, heart beats faster and faster. The violence and danger you encounter you have never seen before. This horror is your limits of humanity. 
Ishimura its not just a ship. It’s a character that wants to tell you a story. A bloody screaming story. But fear…fear is not an option here. You have to put things together and with many handy mining tools that soon becomes your friends. Friends until the end. Plasma Cutter is one of the most bad as weapons ever invented. With this baby you can hit any micro rock from many feets away. Cut, slice or stomp. 
The presentation and visualization of this game is beyond other level. No health bar covering your eyes or ammo counter on right side. Its only you and your engineer suit and thoughts. Soon you start to question your sanity. The enemies don’t sleep cause they can pop up from every shadow of the room. Sometimes its better not to look behind but to shoot first. Three rules applies here: If it moves shoot, if its dead-shoot again, if you think it can be alive still shoot. You start to realise what else they can be throwing at you because the enemies constantly evolving by the minutes. What was with only two spiky tenticles now evolved into undying behemoth. 
14 years passed and this gem is still holds up as one of the best true horror games ever made. What makes it even better is that your character don’t speak. Silent protagonist at its best highlight.
